facts.content: Patient presents with watery diarrhea for 3 days.
Patient reports loose watery stools approximately hourly while awake with no blood.
facts.source_text: Loose watery stools ~hourly while awake; no blood.

facts.content: Patient has intermittent crampy lower midline abdominal pain rated about 6–7 out of 10 during episodes.
facts.source_text: Intermittent crampy lower midline abd pain (~6–7/10 during episodes).

facts.content: Patient reports nausea.
Patient has occasional vomiting, especially after drinking milk.
Patient feels hot and feverish but has not checked their temperature.
Patient is passing urine with decreased frequency.
Patient’s brother has had a similar illness for 5 days.
facts.source_text: Brother with similar illness x5 d.

facts.content: Patient can tolerate fluids but reports that they seem to pass through quickly.
After eating lunch today, the patient had a loose stool.
The duration of watery diarrhea is 3 days.
facts.source_text: Acute gastroenteritis with watery diarrhea x3 d

facts.content: Patient reports being otherwise well with no significant past medical history mentioned.
Patient has recently taken paracetamol.
Patient is on no regular medications.
Patient has no known drug allergies.
Patient’s father has colon cancer reported as stage 3.
facts.source_text: FH: Father with colon cancer (reported stage “3”).

facts.content: Patient lives with mother and sister.
facts.source_text: SH: Lives with mother and sister.

facts.content: Patient works in a government office in Central London.
Patient smokes socially.
Patient drinks alcohol as occasional beers with heavier drinking one to two times per month.
Patient’s work has been impacted by current symptoms.
Patient usually buys food and does not eat with family.
facts.source_text: Usually buys food; doesn’t eat with family.

facts.content: Assessment is acute gastroenteritis with watery diarrhea for 3 days, intermittent lower midline cramps, nausea and vomiting, subjective fever, and contact with brother with similar symptoms.
facts.source_text: 1) Acute gastroenteritis with watery diarrhea x3 d, intermittent lower midline cramps, nausea/vomiting, subjective fever; contact with brother with similar sx.

facts.content: There is no blood in the stool (no hematochezia).
There is a noted risk of dehydration.
Advise oral rehydration therapy with over-the-counter oral rehydration salts such as Dioralyte and to maintain clear fluids.
facts.source_text: • ORT: OTC oral rehydration salts (e.g., Dioralyte); maintain clear fluids.

facts.content: Recommend a soft diet including soups and mashed foods, advancing as tolerated.
facts.source_text: • Diet: Soft diet (soups, mash); advance as tolerated.

facts.content: Use paracetamol as needed for fever or pain.
Patient is advised to avoid alcohol.
If symptoms are not settling in 48 hours or if the patient becomes dehydrated, they should call back as further investigations may be needed.
facts.source_text: • Safety-net: If not settling in 48 h or if becoming dehydrated, call back; may need further Ix.

facts.content: Patient should call back if symptoms are not settling in 48 hours or if signs of dehydration develop, as further investigation may be required.
facts.source_text: • Safety-net: If not settling in 48 h or if becoming dehydrated, call back; may need further Ix.
